previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, COPD, and prior crack cocaine use was admitted for acute shortness of breath and reduced exercise tolerance. He reported orthopnea, leg swelling, and a dry cough, with recent high-salt food intake. Initial evaluation showed pulmonary edema on imaging and elevated BNP, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure. He was treated with IV diuretics and nebulizers in the ED, then required BiPAP for respiratory support and was transferred to the ICU. Due to concern for crack-related pneumonitis, he received a course of steroids and antibiotics. His condition improved with treatment, and he was weaned off BiPAP. Repeat imaging showed resolving pulmonary edema, viral studies were negative, and urine culture showed no infection. He was discharged home with a short course of prednisone, instructions to continue heart and diabetes medications, strict low-salt diet, daily weight monitoring, and close outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year-old male with a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy 
(EF=20%), DM, COPD and multiple admissions for cocaine related 
pneumonitis admitted for respiratory distress after cocaine use. 


# Cocaine Related Pneumonitis: On admission, pt was started on 
standing albuterol  and ipratroprium nebs and prednisone 50mg po 
qday. Antibiotics were intially held, but he received 
Vanc/Cefepime on HD #2 for worsening respiratory status, 
tachypnea and diaphoresis. These antibiotics were discontinued 
on HD #3 when his respiratory status improved with q2h albuterol 
nebs, he remained afebrile and blood cultures were negative. He 
was ruled out for Flu. On ___ pt triggered for tachypnea and 
hypoxia. His O2 was increased to non-rebreather and his O2 sat 
increased from 88% on 50% FiO2 to 97% on NRB. His tachypnea and 
tachycardia initially improved and the patient felt subjectively 
better. Roughly 30 minutes later, he becamse increasingly 
tachycardic to the 160s. His O2 sats dropped on 88% on NRB and 
he was given Ativan and Morphine. The MICU was notified that the 
patient would require transfer for persistent hypoxia. RT was 
called and he was placed on BiPAP. His tachycardia persisted and 
his O2 Sats continued to drop and Code Blue was called. 
Anestehsia arrived and intubated the patient. Tube placement was 
confirmed, but his O2 Sats continued to be in the 60-70s despite 
PEEP 15 on 100% FiO2. He was given Lasix 100mg IV and 
transferred to the MICU. He was never pulseless, no compressions 
or Epi required. In MICU, pt was maintained on low-tidal volume, 
high frequency ARDSnet ventilation and slowly weaned as lung 
compliance improved. Steroids and nebulizers were continued. He 
was extubated to non-invasive ventilation on HD#5 and by HD#6 
was saturating well on nasal cannula. He was then transferred to 
the floor where he was noted to have brisk autodiuresis and was 
quickly weaned from supplemental oxygen.

# Acute on chronic sCHF: Patient has severe systolic CHF due to 
idiopathic cardiomyopathy with LVEF of 15% which was acutely 
decompensated this admission as evidenced by acute pulmonary 
edema in the setting of tachycardia and hypertension to 160/110s 
and HR to 160s. Patient receieved IV lasix boluses and 
metolazone in ICU with poor response and was started on lasix 
gtt with excellent UOP. Diuresis continued after cessation of 
gtt, leading to hypotension likely ___ hypovolemia. Pt was given 
IVF resuscitation w/ improvement in BP. Dry weight per OMR 
appeared to be ~87.5kg, pt 91.8kg on admission, ICU ___. 
Held diuretics after transfer to floor as he had continued brisk 
urine output in the setting of hyperglycemia. On day of 
discharge, pt appeared euvolemic, urine output normalized and 
patient was instructed to restart home torsemide at home the 
following morning.  - Cont digoxin

# IDDM: Uncontrolled, last A1C >8%. On lantus and novalog at 
home.  His BG was very labile during this admission, ranging 
from 30 to 400s in the ICU. His Lantus was initially decreased 
for persistent hypoglycemia and he was placed on standing 
prandial Humalog with ISS. Subsequently had difficult to control 
blood glucose in the setting of high dose prednisone during time 
in ICU and briefly required an insulin drip. After prednisone 
course completed ___ upon transfer to floor, blood sugars began 
to improve and patient was transitioned back to home glargine 
regimen. Fasting blood glucose on day of discharge was 
100s-200s.

# Psych/Substance abuse. Pt has long psych history, reported 
command hallucinations telling him to use drugs. He was 
evaluated by psychiatry who felt that presentation was most 
consistent with a diagnosis of schizophrenia, paranoid type, 
PTSD, and alcohol and cocaine dependence. Anti-psychotic 
medications were deferred pending outpatient followup. 
Appointment was made with patient's regular psychiatrist and 
intake appointment for ___ Dual Diagnosis clinic was arranged.

# Acute renal failure:  Cr peaked at 2 in the setting of acutely 
decompensated ___. Cr gradually improved, home ___ was briefly 
held and restarted on day of discharge at which time Cr was 1. 

# Demand cardiac ischemia: Pt with elevated troponins on 
admission with normal CKMB. EKG was notable for ST depressions 
in V4-V6. He denied CP that was not associated with cough and 
his troponinemia was felt to be related to demand ischemia in 
the setting of CKD. 

# MED REC: Patient was followed by the PACT team in house who 
arranged for patient to have assistance with home medication 
co-pay with pharmacist at his outpatient pharmacy. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
# Cocaine abuse: Planned followup in ___ Dual Diagnosis 
Program, intake appointment ___ at 9am, pt provided with 
___ for transportation to appointment.
# Schizophrenia: Initiation of anti-psychotic medications 
deferred until evaluation at ___ partial program and 
scheduled follow up with regular outpatient psych provider 
# DM: Labile blood sugars during admission in the setting of 
prednisone use, discharged home on previous regimen, will need 
blood glucose checked at follow up

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPHS

HISTORY:  Cough and body ache.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest, PA and lateral.

FINDINGS:  The heart is again mild-to-moderately enlarged.There is new
confluent opacification in the left upper lobe, particularly near the apex
with lesser involvement elsewhere.  To a lesser degree, there is also new
right apical opacification.  A right lower lung opacity is similar to
improved, however.  The lungs are hyperinflated.  There is no pleural effusion
or pneumothorax.  Bony structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Much more extensive lung opacification than seen on the prior
study including confluent left apical opacification with a distribution that
is not typical for pulmonary edema.  An infectious process could be
considered, but the process is widespread but heterogenous, with a strikingly
peripheral distribution in the left upper lobe which could be seen with an
eosinophilic pneumonia, which has been described as a manifestation of
cocaine-related lung disease.  A coinciding component of pulmonary edema is
also possible.

INDICATION:  Likely crack pneumonitis versus COPD flare or pneumonia with
decreased O2 saturations.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable frontal chest radiograph.

FINDINGS:  Cardiac silhouette remains enlarged, unchanged from prior exam. 
Global heterogeneous opacities with a peripheral predilection are worse
compared to ___ with an appearance suggestive of eosinophilic pneumonia. 
There is no pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Worsening bilateral peripheral opacities with a distribution
suggestive of eosinophilic pneumonia.

HISTORY:  ___ male with respiratory failure.  Gastric tube placement
evaluation.

COMPARISON:  Radiographs dated ___, and CT dated ___.

FINDINGS:

Single frontal view of the chest demonstrates interval placement of ET tube
with tip terminating 2.7 cm above the carina.  Compared to 1 day prior, there
is massive progressive worsening of widespread pulmonary opacities and near
complete white-out of bilateral lungs with relative sparing of the right upper
lobe.  There is new obscuration of the cardiac silhouette as well as a
bilateral diaphragmatic contours allowing for which, cardiomegaly is likely
unchanged.  Bilateral effusions may be present.  There is no pneumothorax. 
The airway remains midline.  Note is made of an airdistended stomach.

IMPRESSION:

1.  ET tube with tip terminating 2.7 cm above the carina.

2.  Marked rapid progression of pulmonary disease with now diffuse dense
opacification of bilateral lungs and mild sparing of the right upper lobe,
overall appearance suggestive of ARDS.  

3.  Moderate air distended stomach.  NGT placement should be considered.
